reference: Peter Cundall and Otto Strack, 'A discrete numerical model for granular assemblies', Geotechnique 29, 47 (1979), gave the distinct element method used here: rigid disks, a linear normal spring with a dashpot, a tangential spring capped by Coulomb friction, and an explicit step bounded by the contact period. The settle is not time-accurate at its production step: the restitution coefficient depends on where in a step contact begins, −12.1% to +5.7% of the analytic value at damping ≤ 0.5 (the pre-registered 10% bound was missed); it converges at first order to the analytic contact law.

The top load does not load the packing: at photo, strong and slip the lid carries at most 3.4% of the weight at any step and nothing at the end, so presets with a top load, and the periodic sides only they use, are outside the domain.

The starting lattice overlaps (255 to 562 pairs, up to 1.29 r0), so every packing is prepared by an explosive decompression and settling, not a pour. The same seed settles to a different packing in Node and Chromium because Math.cos differs by one ulp between them; each engine reprints its own packing exactly.

No Radjai force-distribution, Janssen, photoelastic or experimental claim: side-wall friction carries −6.2% to +7.0% of the weight depending on history, and the column preset carries −0.1% in its printed packing. Broader settings require additional independent evidence.

numerical.criteria: Fixed before the first run and committed first. Collisions: e and contact duration within 0.5% of the no-tension analytic values at h/64 in every case; refinement to h/64 reduces the e error tenfold or below 0.1%; e within 10% at the production step for damping ≤ 0.5; the tensile formula off by more than ten times the clamped error at damping ≥ 0.2; e identical (1e-9) across hardness. Friction: displacements within 1%, stick time within 2% plus two steps, no slip beyond the elastic range of the tangential spring after sticking or below the incline threshold, total slip within 3% above it, |J_t/J_n| and the slip change within 2% of μ and 3J_t/m_eff. Statics: vertical and horizontal wall balance within 1% of the floor load, dashpot share of the normal forces below 1%, kinetic energy below the module's at-rest threshold, contacts, backbone and Z identical and the other status quantities within 1e-12 of a brute-force rebuild; Z bands [3.8, 4.6], [3.0, 4.0], [2.8, 3.6] at friction 0, 0.4, 0.8, separated by more than 3 standard errors; column side walls carry more than 5% of the weight. Misses (production e for rmin–rmax at damping 0.5, −10.6%; incline slip at tan θ/3μ = 1.05, +8.7% at every friction) are recorded and reproduced exactly; follow-ups with criteria fixed before they ran test their causes.
numerical.benchmark: The linear spring–dashpot with the F_n ≥ 0 clamp has e = exp(−ζω0 t_c), ω_d t_c = π − 2 asin ζ (Schwager and Pöschel, Granular Matter 9, 465 (2007)); rigid-disk Coulomb friction with I = m r²/2 (sliding to rolling, the incline threshold tan θ = 3μ, and impulse theory in gross sliding) including the module's background drag; Newton's static balance of the settled packing against the total weight; isostatic coordination (4 without friction, falling toward 3 with it); a brute-force contact rebuild for the status line.
numerical.failureControl: A flipped dashpot sign (e = 2.475 against 0.404) and a dashpot allowed to pull (e = 0.309, the tensile value) fail the collision criteria; wall friction off, a flipped wall torque, incline friction off and a flipped torque on the second grain of a pair (slip change −66.7%) fail the friction criteria; a settle cut to 5% of its budget (vertical residual 116%), gravity on the mean mass (5.9%) and a Verlet list that is never rebuilt (36165 contacts missing) fail the statics.
numerical.limitations: Contact tests isolate one or two disks through a hand-built D. reference: Oded Schramm, Israel Journal of Mathematics 118, 221 (2000), 'Scaling limits of loop-erased random walks and uniform spanning trees'. Charles Loewner's 1923 equation grows a curve into the upper half plane from a real driving function; Schramm showed that the only conformally invariant random curves with the domain Markov property come from driving it with Brownian motion of variance κ, and identified κ with the critical models whose interfaces they describe. Gregory Lawler, Schramm and Wendelin Werner computed the exponents; Stanislav Smirnov proved the percolation case. The curve is computed here as a composition of vertical slit maps, after Tom Kennedy, Journal of Statistical Physics 137, 839 (2009).

reference: Lionel Levine and Yuval Peres, 'Strong spherical asymptotics for rotor-router aggregation and the divisible sandpile', Potential Analysis 30, 1 (2009), is the theorem this plate measures. For an aggregate of n particles in d dimensions, written as n = ω_d r^d, they prove the inradius is at least r − O(log r) and the outradius at most r + O(r^α) for every α > 1 − 1/d, which in the plane is r + O(r^α) for every α > 1/2. The two sides of that sandwich are not the same strength, and the plate does not pretend they are: the inner bound is logarithmic and proved, the outer bound proved here is a power, and the status line reports what this lattice actually measures rather than what the tighter of the two would suggest. There is no probability anywhere in the statement. The rotor-router walk and the aggregation model are James Propp's; they are studied in Ander Holroyd and James Propp, 'Rotor walks and Markov chains', Contemporary Mathematics 520 (2010), and in Joshua Cooper and Joel Spencer, 'Simulating a random walk with constant error', Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 15 (2006). Internal diffusion limited aggregation, the random counterpart drawn beside it, is Gregory Lawler, Maury Bramson and David Griffeath, 'Internal diffusion limited aggregation', Annals of Probability 20, 2117 (1992), who proved its limit shape is a disk; David Jerison, Lionel Levine and Scott Sheffield, Journal of the American Mathematical Society 25, 271 (2012), showed its fluctuations are logarithmic as well, so the gap the plate measures between the two is one of constants and of certainty, not of orders. That a finished aggregate does not depend on the order the particles were routed in is the abelian property of Persi Diaconis and William Fulton, Rendiconti del Seminario Matematico dell'Università e del Politecnico di Torino (1991); it is the same argument Deepak Dhar, Physical Review Letters 64, 1613 (1990), made for the abelian sandpile of Per Bak, Chao Tang and Kurt Wiesenfeld, Physical Review Letters 59, 381 (1987).

numerical.criteria: A state with Boltzmann probability at least 1e-4 is scored on its own; the rest are one pooled tail, so all 256 frequencies enter the comparison. Pass when every scored |z| is at most 4, the tail |z| is at most 4, and |sum z^2 - k| is at most 4*sqrt(2k). This run meets the gate: sum z^2 = 174.1 over 162, 171.2 over 121 and 254.5 over 254, max |z| = 3.46. The (1.6, 0.55, 0.3) sum is 3.23 standard deviations above 121 on an independent chi-squared scale, inside the gate. A sweep at twice the temperature, and a sweep that ignores the energy and keeps each flip with probability 1/2, both miss the gate with some scored |z| above 4.
numerical.limitations: The 2x2 torus only, three parameter points, below the UI grid minimum. Consecutive frames are not independent; the gate is the batch-mean z. States below probability 1e-4 are not scored individually. This tool does not print. Not Lieb's residual entropy and not the status-line monopole weight.
numerical.benchmark: The Boltzmann weight exp(-E/T) of every orientation of the 2x2 torus, E = (J/2) sum Q^2 - h sum sigma from the plate's own charges(), divided by the explicit 256-state partition function. Scripted single flips check that this energy is the one the plate's accept and reject use, including a nonzero field.
numerical.failureControl: Run the plate's own sweep on the 2x2 torus and compare all 256 state frequencies with exp(-E/T) by batch means, 200 batches. States with probability at least 1e-4 are scored one by one; the rest are one pooled tail. Calling that sweep at twice the temperature misses the gate, and so does a copy of the module that ignores the energy and keeps each flip with probability 1/2. The plate's Metropolis update is the sampler being measured, not the failure. Consecutive frames are not independent, so the z scores use the batch variances.

reference: Christopher Klausmeier, Science 284, 1826 (1999). Water w rains in at rate a, evaporates, runs downhill at speed v and is taken up by plants n in proportion to n², because roots make the soil take water faster. Plants die at rate m and spread slowly. On a slope the model makes bands of vegetation perpendicular to the flow that creep uphill: the tiger bush of Niger, Australia and the Horn of Africa seen from the air. Diffusion of water is not in the original; here it is a small optional term.
equation: ∂w/∂t = a − w − w n² + v ∂w/∂x + D_w∇²w,   ∂n/∂t = w n² − m n + ∇²n
limitations: Catalog equation and citation are review targets, not verified paper equivalence.
Complete evidence covers only the documented domain in validation/RDX.md and validation/results/rdx-science.json plus paused-initial print preservation in validation/results/rdx-print-state.json.
Linear regime and uniform states only within this domain; float32 implicit denominator 1 + dt quantizes water loss (modelled in the discrete reference).

Time step: from recipe v5 the step is at most 0.8 of the combined explicit bound 2/(Q D_w c^2 + 2 v c) of the water row, and of the plant row. Recipes made before v5 keep the pre-v5 step where it was under the bare-soil bound 2/(R - 1), so they reprint, and take the combined step where it was not, which corrects plates that were growing grid-scale checkerboards. Kept pre-v5 steps can lie within 0.03% of the bound at the corner of the ranges (validation/PDE-ORDER.md). The bound is linear and frozen-coefficient, not a nonlinear stability proof.
No Float16 fallback, noise, nonlinear pattern-selection statistics, spiral/band spacing claims, evolved/running exports, or universal hardware claim.
Broader settings require additional independent evidence.

reference: Noam Elkies, Greg Kuperberg, Michael Larsen and James Propp, Journal of Algebraic Combinatorics 1, 111 and 219 (1992), counted the domino tilings of the Aztec diamond of order n (there are 2^{n(n+1)/2}) and gave the shuffling algorithm that samples one uniformly. William Jockusch, James Propp and Peter Shor, 'Random domino tilings and the arctic circle theorem' (1998), proved that a uniformly random tiling is frozen outside the inscribed circle and disordered inside it. James Propp, Theoretical Computer Science 303, 267 (2003), on generalized domino shuffling.
equation: order n → n+1: delete colliding pairs, slide N↑ S↓ W← E→, fill each empty 2×2 block with a random pair
limitations: The tab's frozen regions are the theorem's polar regions (a domino connected to the boundary through edge-adjacent dominoes of its own type, as Johansson 2005 states the definition of Jockusch, Propp and Shor); they equal an independent union-find on all 2,350 arctic plates. The earlier local test read 0.2778 +/- 0.0009 in the limit, 67 sigma above 1 - pi/4.

The status line's per-plate error bar is the standard error of the free cells summed over 60 angular sectors, from their integrated autocorrelation time (window closed at the first non-positive autocorrelation, floored at 2, capped at 15). The scatter of the printed fraction over seeds is 0.83 to 0.91 of it at orders 40 to 320, inside the calibration band 0.75 to 1.33 fixed before the run, but conservative, overstating the scatter by 10 to 20 per cent with 95 per cent intervals that exclude 1: the truncated window leaves out a negative autocorrelation lobe and the four-fold mean pattern of the sector counts enters each plate's variance. The bar is not calibrated below order 40, although the UI starts at 8. The status line says so at those orders.

The spread of the four polar regions, the bar it replaced, was too wide: the scatter was 0.68 to 0.88 of it because neighboring regions are anticorrelated (-0.28 at order 40 to -0.06 at 320); the estimator was chosen on a separate training family of 1,950 plates, not on the tool's seeds.

Exact uniformity is established by exhaustive enumeration only at orders 1 to 5, run through the tab's build() and shuffle() below the UI range of 8 to 320; larger orders are tested only through the arctic boundary statistics.

The polar-region area and the axis radius agree with 1 - pi/4 and 1/sqrt(2) only after extrapolation in n with the stated form q_inf + A n^-2/3 + B n^-1 (0.2127 +/- 0.0013, -1.5 sigma; 0.7097 +/- 0.0016, +1.7 sigma); a two-parameter n^-2/3 fit over orders 113 to 320 gives +1.4 and -2.6 sigma, so the agreement holds at about 0.003 in area and 0.005 in radius, and at order 320 the polar area is still 0.030 above its limit. Since 2026-09-29 the status line compares the polar fraction with the exact expectation at that order, not with the limit. The expectation in the browser is the same Krawtchouk formula, held to the research values within 1e-5 by tools/arctic-exact-check.js.
Uniformity probabilities assume the seeded U.makeRng streams behave as independent uniform draws; fixed PRNG samples do not prove it.
Print evidence covers five recipes on one renderer (headless Chromium 141, SwiftShader, Linux). Grain is a raster finish that the vector print omits.
remaining: Extend print evidence to other renderers and more recipes; extend exhaustive uniformity beyond order 5 only with a different method (the count is 2^{n(n+1)/2}).

reference: N. Hatano and D. R. Nelson, Phys. Rev. Lett. 77, 570 (1996), wrote a directed-hopping chain whose bulk spectrum is that of Hermitian tight-binding while every eigenvector piles onto a boundary. Yao and Wang, Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 086803 (2018), named this the non-Hermitian skin effect and showed it breaks the usual bulk-boundary correspondence. Hermitian quantum mechanics cannot do it: a similarity transform that is not unitary has no counterpart when H = H†.
limitations: Evidence is the open chain with on-site disorder below 0.04, where the plate is the closed form and not a diagonalization. Disordered and periodic paths use subspace iteration with Gram-Schmidt and are not right eigenvectors. They are excluded.

Finite N only. Eigenvalues must match 2 cos(pi n/(N+1)) to 1e-8 and sign-aligned right eigenvectors must match the closed form to 1e-6, both checked for N <= 48. The tab's Float32 densities match that ED reference to 1e-6 on grids 48, 64 and 96. No infinite-volume or laboratory claim.

The probability length 1/(2|g|) is a regression test, not a prediction: once the right eigenvectors match e^{g j} sin(pi n j/(N+1)), the log ratio of |psi|^2 on sine-conjugate sites is forced by the closed form, so the length follows. It is read from the log slope of |psi|^2 on sine-conjugate sites, not the amplitude length 1/|g| and not the mean distance from the right end. That mean is shifted by the boundary node (14.41 sites for N=64, g=0.08, mode 1, against a probability length of 6.25).

The default plate draws at most one row per mode. On this source, grid 96 and aspect 4:5 is 96 rows and skin weight 0.780, the same modes as aspect 1:1 (validation/results/skin-rows.json). Recipes before v8 keep the sheet height, 120 rows and weight 0.773 on that sheet, and the status line says so. Those old recipes are outside this claim.

The Chromium print covers two open clean fixtures on this source, both grid 96, g = 0.08, disorder 0, log view, 96 by 96 cells: aspect 4:5 at 1920 by 2400 (111595 bytes) and aspect 1:1 at 2400 by 2400 (128100 bytes). Both report skin weight 0.779865. Colour is not calibrated. Disordered and periodic paths are not printed.
remaining: A right-eigenvector treatment of on-site disorder and of periodic ends is still open. The Gram-Schmidt path is not validated.

reference: Eugene Wigner's semicircle law, Annals of Mathematics 62, 548 (1955), and Freeman Dyson's threefold way and Brownian-motion model, J. Math. Phys. 3, 140 and 1191 (1962). The tridiagonal matrix models that make a general β cheap to sample are Ioana Dumitriu and Alan Edelman, 'Matrix models for beta ensembles', J. Math. Phys. 43, 5830 (2002). The status line compares the spacing spread with the exact Gaudin-Mehta law (Michel Mehta, Random Matrices), evaluated as Fredholm determinants by Folkmar Bornemann's method, Math. Comp. 79, 871 (2010); Wigner's surmise is its 2×2 approximation. The gamma sampler is George Marsaglia and Wai Wan Tsang, ACM TOMS 26, 363 (2000).
equation: p(λ) ∝ ∏_{i<j} |λ_i − λ_j|^β · e^{−Σλ_i²/4};   Dyson (β = 1): dλ_i = √2 dB_i + (Σ_{j≠i} 1/(λ_i − λ_j) − λ_i/2) dt
limitations: Complete evidence covers only the domain in validation/RMT.md: sampler, solver and exact moments for n 24-400 and beta 0.1-12, semicircle for beta 1-12, Gaudin-Mehta spacing law at beta 1 and 2 with n 400, the printed spread of two presets, Dyson mode at 24 paths, and five complete prints.

The code samples the Dumitriu-Edelman matrix without its 1/sqrt(2), so the eigenvalue density is exp(-sum l^2/4); since 2026-09-24 the displayed equation says so, and it shows the Dyson mode's -l/2 Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift at beta = 1.

At n 150 the local unfolding (24-gap window) biases the spacing scale: the CV agrees with Gaudin-Mehta but the pooled KS distance (0.0043, 0.0044) exceeds its bootstrap critical value (0.0027, 0.0025). The spacing-distribution claim is limited to n 400.

Since 2026-09-24 the status line prints the unfolded CV through compare() with its row-bootstrap error against the exact Gaudin-Mehta values (0.53435 at beta 1, 0.42426 at beta 2), with the Wigner surmise as a note; at beta 1 the tab's own sample resolves the surmise's 0.012 error. Only beta 1 and 2 have an exact reference in the status line.
Finite samples from one seeded PRNG; error bars assume independent draws. Beta 4 spacings, edge statistics, beta outside 0.05-20 and the sweep plate's printed spread are not tested.

reference: The sampler is James Propp and David Wilson, 'Exact sampling with coupled Markov chains and applications to statistical mechanics', Random Structures and Algorithms 9, 223 to 252 (1996); random tilings are one of their own worked examples. The limit shape measured on the plate is Henry Cohn, Michael Larsen and James Propp, 'The shape of a typical boxed plane partition', New York Journal of Mathematics 4, 137 to 165 (1998). The count of boxed plane partitions is Percy MacMahon, 'Memoir on the theory of the partitions of numbers, Part VI: partitions in two-dimensional space, to which is added an adumbration of the theory of partitions in three-dimensional space', Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A 211, 345 to 373 (1912). The height function that turns a tiling into a stack of cubes is William Thurston, 'Conway's tiling groups', American Mathematical Monthly 97, 757 to 773 (1990). How long this chain needs is David Wilson, 'Mixing times of lozenge tiling and card shuffling Markov chains', Annals of Applied Probability 14, 274 to 325 (2004). The frozen test is the lozenge form of the polar regions of William Jockusch, James Propp and Peter Shor, 'Random domino tilings and the arctic circle theorem' (1998), as Kurt Johansson states them in 'The arctic circle boundary and the Airy process', Annals of Probability 33, 1 (2005).
equation: h(x, y) ∈ [0, c] weakly decreasing;  heat bath h(x, y) ~ U{max(h(x+1,y), h(x,y+1)) … min(h(x−1,y), h(x,y−1))};  run −T → 0 from ⊥ and ⊤ on one fixed set of maps, doubling T until they agree, and read the common value at 0
limitations: Since recipe v4 a rhombus is frozen when a chain of edge-adjacent rhombi of its own orientation joins it to the rim, the lozenge analogue of the Jockusch-Propp-Shor polar regions (as Johansson 2005 states them) adopted by analogy; Cohn, Larsen and Propp state their theorem for the height function, and the definition is not quoted from them. The module's flags equal an independent union-find over rhombi and the extreme level sets of the height function on all 2,720 limit-shape plates.

At every size the tab offers an exact plate reads below the limit shape on the radius, about seven of its own error bars on a regular hexagon (radius 0.9085 at 12, 12, 12 and 0.9663 at 48, 48, 48), because the frozen regions reach one to one and a half tiles past the ellipse; the status line names this finite-size cause for the radius. Since 2026-09-29 the free area, when the frozen test is the rim-connected one, is compared with the exact expectation at that box. The Monte Carlo free areas 0.7516 and 0.8473 agree with that expectation (0.751050 and 0.847603) within their error bars. Agreement of those areas with the limit 0.9069 holds only after extrapolation with the stated form q_inf + A n^-2/3 + B n^-1: free area 0.9005 +/- 0.0052 (-1.2 sigma) and radius 0.9949 +/- 0.0033 (-1.5 sigma) for regular hexagons 12 to 48; 0.866 +/- 0.032 and 0.984 +/- 0.020 for the 3:5:6 family, whose three-parameter fit has one degree of freedom. The two-parameter form moves the regular limits by 0.006 in area and 0.007 in radius, well inside 3 sigma of the limit either way.

The n^(1/3) boundary scale behind that form is assumed by analogy with the Aztec diamond; the spread of the corner depth grows as n^0.248 +/- 0.030 over sizes 12 to 48, 2.8 sigma below 1/3, with depths of only 3 to 8 cells.

Both per-plate error bars (integrated autocorrelation time over 60 angular sectors, the free area now included) are checked against the scatter over seeds at the eleven hexagons measured, which is 0.77 to 1.03 of the bar, inside the band 0.75 to 1.33 fixed before the run; they are about right at 40 and 48 a side and overstate the scatter by up to 30 per cent elsewhere, and the lowest ratio, 0.77 at 12, 20, 24, is near the lower edge of the band. Lopsided boxes such as 48, 48, 8 and all other shapes are outside the calibrated domain.

The local radius 1 to 4 tests remain for recipes made before v4 (legacy ring 3) and are not the arctic boundary: on the same tilings radius 3 extrapolates 6.6 sigma below the limit in both radius and free area.

Exhaustive uniformity covers the boxes 2,2,2, 2,2,3, 2,3,4 and 3,3,3 plus the volume law on 4,4,4; larger hexagons use the same code but are not enumerated here. Uniformity probabilities assume the seeded draws behave as independent uniform variates; fixed PRNG samples do not prove it.

reference: S. D. Poisson argued in 1818 that Fresnel's wave theory implied a bright spot on axis in the shadow of an opaque disk, which he took as a reductio. D. F. J. Arago performed the experiment and found the spot. The plate is a Fresnel propagator through a circular stop.
equation: U(0) = (e^{ikz}/iλz) ∫_{|ρ|>R} exp(ik|ρ|²/2z) dρ,   I(0) ≃ I_open
limitations: The checked claim is the Fresnel (paraxial) identity for a circular disk and its complementary circular aperture: I_disk(0)/I_open(0) = 1 and I_aperture(0)/I_open(0) = 4 sin^2(k R^2 / 4z). It is not a vector diffraction calculation and not a laboratory plate.

The open beam is the integral of this kernel over the whole plane, which the prefactor k/(i z) makes exactly 1. The disk is that beam minus a Simpson integral over the disk only (Babinet). The production on-axis sample uses 16 points per shortest cycle; the painted radii use 8. At 16 points the on-axis disk error is 2.7e-4.

At the defaults the Fresnel number is 207 and the spot's first dark ring is 0.048 cell from the axis, so the painted cells do not resolve the spot. The status line is the on-axis sample, not a cell average. Across the sliders the Fresnel number runs from about 3.6 to about 8000; only the low end is wider than a cell.
Recipes older than v7 keep the aliased cutoff (propagator pre7). At the defaults its center-to-ring ratio is 1.826, which is not I(0)/I_open, and the status line says so.

The Chromium print at 2400x2400 matches an independent paint of the field and changes no field word. On the default plate the preserved metric is 1.000269 and the center cell is 0.00849, because the spot radius is 0.048 cell: the pixels are not I(0). At the low-Fresnel corner, F = 3.62, four cells lie inside the first dark ring and the brightest is 0.293, not the on-axis sample. The pre-v7 sheet preserves a center/ring ratio of 1.826 and fails the Poisson predicate.
remaining: The painted cells miss the spot over most of the slider range. The widest spot the sliders allow is 1.06 cells, and those cells are not the on-axis sample.

numerical.criteria: At 16 points per cycle, |I_disk(0)/I_open - 1| < 1e-3 and |I_aperture(0)/I_open - 4 sin^2(k R^2/4z)| < 1e-3 on every listed point (measured disk error 2.69e-4 at the defaults, 1.000269). asksForOne, abs(ratio-1) <= 0.01, passes for that disk and fails for the aperture whenever the closed form is more than 0.05 from 1 (defaults aperture 2.0469 against 2.0467). Samples 4 at the defaults fails asksForOne (error 0.0966) and the error falls at each doubling. Off-axis disk errors 1.7e-6 and 5.8e-6. The pre-v7 center/ring ratio is 1.826 and fails asksForOne. reference: David Bruce Wilson, 'Generating random spanning trees more quickly than the cover time', Proceedings of the 28th ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing, 296 (1996), is the algorithm drawn here: cycle popping by loop-erased random walk, exact rather than approximate, with the expected cost determined by root-dependent commute times. Those are Andrei Broder, 'Generating random spanning trees', 30th Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science, 442 (1989), and David Aldous, SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics 3, 450 (1990). The loop-erased walk itself is Gregory Lawler, Duke Mathematical Journal 47, 655 (1980). Lawler, Oded Schramm and Wendelin Werner, Annals of Probability 32, 939 (2004), proved that the loop-erased walk scales to SLE with κ = 2 and the tree's Peano curve to SLE with κ = 8. That every spanning tree of a graph can be counted at all is Gustav Kirchhoff, Annalen der Physik 148, 497 (1847).
equation: pick v ∉ T, walk at random from v erasing each loop as it closes, attach the surviving path;  P(T) = 1 / κ(G) for every one of the κ(G) spanning trees

The Custom potential mode steps a potential V(x, y) the viewer types, with coefficients a and b, through the same leapfrog. A user-defined potential is not validated: the status line says so and prints no comparison with theory in that mode, the stage badge and the provenance read unvalidated, and none of the evidence above covers it. V is sampled once per cell in double precision on the CPU (x and y from the frame center in units of half its shorter side, y up), stored at the state precision, held between -16 and 16, and a cell where it is undefined (NaN) is a hard wall. The step used is min(dt, 1.6/(4 + max|V|)) over the stored samples, the bound this record states for every potential (validation/SCHRODINGER.md, Custom potential). That bound keeps the explicit scheme stable; it says nothing about accuracy: the lattice dispersion and a potential that changes over a few cells are resolved only as well as the grid allows.

reference: W. P. Su, J. R. Schrieffer and A. J. Heeger, Phys. Rev. Lett. 42, 1698 (1979), on dimerised polyacetylene. The winding of the Bloch Hamiltonian in the Brillouin zone is a topological invariant; when it is 1 an open chain hosts a zero mode at each end, inside the bulk gap. Periodic boundaries have nowhere to put them. The plate is |ψ_n(x)|² of every eigenmode of the finite chain, energy increasing upward, each row scaled to its own peak; the mid-gap pair sits in the middle rows.
equation: H = v Σ_i (a†_i b_i + h.c.) + w Σ_i (b†_i a_{i+1} + h.c.),   ν = 1 for w > v (open)
limitations: The studio solver is compared with an independent Float64 Jacobi solve on every registered preset (N = 96, and Critical at N = 160). Other grids, the plate's row mapping, per-row scaling and palette are not compared pixel by pixel. Print evidence is that exportPNG leaves the Float32 mode field, end weight, energy, cells and settings unchanged; it is not a pixel match to the Jacobi modes. No interactions or experiment.

The end weight and the verdict are measured from the eigenvectors of one finite chain and carry no sampling error; they are finite-size quantities with a fixed 10% window at each end. Mid-gap energies under 1e-13 are not resolved in double precision and are printed as a bound. Critical (w/v 1.06) reads crossover at the default 96 sites, because its localisation length of 18.5 cells is comparable to the 48-cell chain; at 160 sites it reads edge modes.

Until 2026-09-24 the intra hopping was keyed v, which the engine overwrites with the recipe version (2). Every plate opened from a hash, a preset, Surprise or a reload therefore ran at v = 2 and drew the trivial picture whatever the controls said. Dragging the slider changed the plate on screen, but its hash still recorded only v = 2. The key is now vIntra. A hash written before the rename never stored the intra hopping, so it reprints at the default 0.45 with its stored w, and its pixels change.

reference: Elsen Tjhung, Cesare Nardini and Michael E. Cates, Physical Review X 8, 031080 (2018). Cahn-Hilliard describes a passive mixture relaxing toward equilibrium. Two extra gradient terms, λ|∇φ|² in the chemical potential and a current ζ(∇²φ)∇φ that cannot come from any free energy, are the leading ways an active system (motile bacteria, self-propelled colloids) can break time-reversal symmetry while still conserving φ. They give the two phases different interfacial tensions, and when the tension felt by the minority phase turns negative the Ostwald process runs backward: large droplets shed material to small ones and coarsening stops.

reference: S. Aubry and G. André, Ann. Israel Phys. Soc. 3, 133 (1980). A quasiperiodic potential is deterministic, yet past λ = 1 every eigenstate localizes. With unit hopping the potential is 2λ cos(2π β n), and the model is self-dual: momentum-space at λ is real-space at 1/λ, so the transition sits exactly at 1. The plate shows a finite periodic golden-ratio chain after a fixed number of imaginary-time steps; convergence to its ground state is not established.

reference: Per Bak, Chao Tang and Kurt Wiesenfeld, Phys. Rev. Lett. 59, 381 (1987); Deepak Dhar, Phys. Rev. Lett. 64, 1613 (1990). Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld dropped grains one at a time on a lattice with a toppling threshold and found avalanches of every size, a power law with no tuning: self-organized criticality. Dhar showed the toppling operators commute, so the final stable state does not depend on the order of toppling, and the recurrent configurations form an Abelian group. The identity of that group, computed on a square, is the fractal plate in the second mode.
equation: if hᵢ ≥ 4: hᵢ −= 4, hⱼ += 1 for each neighbor j;   identity e = (2m − (2m)°)°, m = all 3

The recurrent count does not detect a threshold raised to five while toppling still removes four grains (that model is the sandpile shifted by one grain); the stability range check does.

Fixed 2026-09-24: the status line's topplings and random-drop avalanche numbers counted pops of floor(h/4) topplings (and, for the single-source pile, only the octant's own cells), so they undercounted and depended on toppling order. The function is typed by the viewer: the plate renders whatever f the expression language accepts, and nothing checks it against any source. The GPU evaluates f in 32-bit floats, so phase and modulus lose accuracy near zeros, poles, overflow and cancellation; atan(0, 0) and points on a branch cut are left to the GPU, which may take either side of a cut.

The argument-principle count is a double-precision sampled computation, not interval arithmetic: 4096 initial circle samples, with bisection when the wrapped phase change or the angular step times the endpoint logarithmic-derivative magnitude exceeds pi/2. The derivative uses f(theta +/- 1e-7); all probes count toward the 400,000-evaluation budget, with at most 24 refinement levels. Finite differences and endpoint sampling cannot certify arbitrary typed functions or exclude every hidden turn. The argument principle requires a meromorphic function inside and on the circle.

No count or verdict is printed for nonfinite evaluations, a sampled min |f| at or below 1e-9 of max |f|, or unresolved refinement. Conservative refusal includes the tested near-double-zero circles whose analytic count is zero. Essential singularities and branch points inside remain outside the theorem; an accepted number there is only a sampled winding number.
The shading styles and line spacing follow the descriptions of enhanced phase portraits; they have not been compared figure by figure with the cited sources.

Flipping the (2,2) entry from -i*gamma to +i*gamma yields eigenvalues i*gamma +/- kappa. At gamma = kappa = 1 the separation is 2 and the eigenvector overlap is 0, so the coalescence predicate that passes for the PT matrix fails. On the 1,935-point flipped lattice the overlap stays under 1.6e-15.

reference: Roger Penrose, Pentaplexity, 1974, and Martin Gardner's Mathematical Games, January 1977. Robinson triangles carry the deflation; N. G. de Bruijn's dual multigrid (1981) gives the octagonal Ammann–Beenker and dodecagonal cases. The hat — a single 13-sided polykite that tiles the plane only aperiodically, and only with its reflection — is Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss, arXiv:2303.10798 (March 2023). The spectre is the chiral 14-gon from the same authors, arXiv:2305.17743: one handedness, no mirrors.
equation: Penrose: thick half → 2 thick + 1 thin;   hat: 13-gon + mirror;   spectre: 14-gon, one handedness

Defect, P3 matching arcs (src/modules/tilings.js:31): the thin-rhomb arcs sit around the acute corners, both in one family. reference: S. R. Broadbent and J. M. Hammersley, Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 53, 629 (1957); J. Hoshen and R. Kopelman, Phys. Rev. B 14, 3438 (1976); Harry Kesten, Comm. Math. Phys. 74, 41 (1980). Broadbent and Hammersley asked how a fluid spreads through a random porous medium and found a sharp threshold: below p_c every cluster is finite, above it one cluster spans the lattice. Kesten proved the bond threshold on the square lattice is exactly 1/2. The site threshold, about 0.592746, is known only numerically. Hoshen and Kopelman gave the one-pass labeling that finds the clusters.
equation: site occupied iff rᵢ < p;   bond open iff rᵢⱼ < p;   p_c(site) ≈ 0.5927,   p_c(bond) = 1/2

reference: M. V. Berry and N. L. Balazs, Am. J. Phys. 47, 264 (1979). A free Schrödinger (or paraxial Helmholtz) packet is not supposed to accelerate: there is no force. The Airy packet does, its intensity maximum riding the parabola x = z²/4, a consequence of the linear potential in the Airy ODE rather than of a force in the wave equation. Siviloglou, Broky, Dogariu and Christodoulides, Phys. Rev. Lett. 99, 213901 (2007), flew one in the lab. The plate is the exact finite-energy Airy beam, not a cannonball.
equation: ψ(x,z) = Ai(x − z²/4 + i a) exp(a x − a z²/2 + i(x z/2 − z³/12)),   x_peak = z²/4
limitations: Precision check of the real-argument Ai that airy.js actually evaluates (80-step RK4 on [-10, 8], one-term asymptotic for z>8, leading oscillation for z<-10). Not a check of the catalog factor Ai(x - z^2/4 + i a), and not a print audit.

On [-4, 4] the module matches an independent power series to 7.23e-7. The RK4 bridge has the wrong sign at arguments 6 to 8: at z=6 the module returns -1.200e-4 against the series +9.948e-6, and at z=8 it returns -0.07551 against 4.74e-8. The switch to the asymptotic is z>8, so z=8 is still on that bridge. At span 14 the plate coordinate xx reaches span*0.48, about 6.7, so those arguments are on the sheet.

The plate multiplies real Ai by exp(a x - a z^2/2). That is not the finite-energy factor Ai(xi + i a) named in the credit. At a=0.08, |Ai(xi+ia)|/|Ai(xi)| is 1.0017 at xi=0 and 1.030 at xi=-2. The tracked peaks match the real formula, but the mean |peak x - z^2/4| is about 0.89 to 0.95 because the maximum of Ai is near argument -1.02, not 0.

reference: Douglas R. Hofstadter, Phys. Rev. B 14, 2239 (1976). A Bloch electron in a square lattice with perpendicular flux α (in flux quanta per plaquette) has a spectrum that is a fractal in the (α, E) plane — the butterfly. Gaps carry Chern numbers; Avron colored them. At rational α=p/q the Harper matrix is q×q.
equation: ψₙ₊₁ + ψₙ₋₁ + 2 cos(2π n α) ψₙ = E ψₙ
limitations: Evidence is the finite check in validation/HOFSTADTER.md. It is not a laboratory quantum Hall measurement. No edge states, disorder, interactions or continuum Landau level.

The plate draws one phase, θ = φ = 0, so q eigenvalues per rational, not the filled magnetic bands. E -> -E holds for the Bloch Hamiltonian and fails for that single phase when q is odd (at q = 3 the plate is about -2, -0.732, 2.732).

The label is the default symmetric QL. Recipes older than v8 keep the capped Jacobi on the overwritten matrix: q = 1 returns 1, q = 2 returns ±√5, and at q = 8 the error is 0.087. Those plates are outside this label.

The Chern view paints eigenvalue index r with the TKNN integer t_r of the gap below it (r bands filled), not with that band's Chern number. The source comment says the gap below. Density-smear neighbors are painted as Hall integer 0. Node gap-integer checks stop at q = 24. The Chromium Chern sheets check Q = 8, 12 and the preset Q = 28. Above that, the record is eigenvalues only.
At α = 1/4 the middle gap closes. Only the outer bands were compared with the lattice Chern number. The negative tie t_2 = -2 is not an open-gap invariant.
remaining: Sample the Bloch phases if the picture is meant to be the filled butterfly rather than one slice.

reference: K. Weierstrass, presented to the Prussian Academy in 1872 (published 1875). Analysts had assumed a continuous function was differentiable except at isolated points; Weierstrass wrote a Fourier series that is continuous everywhere and differentiable nowhere. Hardy (1916) weakened the condition to ab ≥ 1. The plate uses a finite, seeded phase-shifted sum inspired by that series. Each finite sum is smooth; the classical infinite-series theorem is not established for this displayed field.

reference: A. Yu. Kitaev, Phys.-Usp. 44, 131 (2001). A 1D p-wave superconductor hosts two Majorana operators, one at each end, that together make a single nonlocal fermion. They sit at zero energy, inside the gap, and are their own antiparticles. The plate is computed: the 2N × 2N Bogoliubov-de Gennes matrix of an open chain of N sites, one per column, is diagonalized exactly in double precision (Householder reduction and implicit QL, after Wilkinson and Reinsch, 1971), and each row is |u(x)|² + |v(x)|² of one ± pair of quasiparticle modes, scaled to its own peak, on a linear |E| axis from zero at the top.
equation: H = −μ Σ c†c − t Σ (c†_i c_{i+1}+h.c.) + Δ Σ (c_i c_{i+1}+h.c.),   |μ|<2t ⇒ unpaired γ_L, γ_R
limitations: Complete evidence covers the finite domain in validation/KITAEV.md: mean-field BdG Kitaev chains of 96 to 160 sites in the studio (the grids the tab allows), open in the tab and periodic or antiperiodic in the band check; shorter chains only in the Node tests of the module code.

Splittings below about 4Nε‖H‖ (1e-13 to 4e-13) are not resolved by double precision and are flagged; for most topological presets the exact splitting is far below that. An exact finite-N splitting is used only at Δ = t; elsewhere the rate and oscillation are tested, not the prefactor.
No self-consistent Δ, interactions, disorder, spin or nanowire experiment.
remaining: An exact finite-N splitting for general Δ (for example the closed forms of Leumer et al., J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 32, 445502, 2020) would turn the rate test into a value test.
Disorder and multi-band chains are outside this review.

reference: V. G. Veselago, Sov. Phys. Usp. 10, 509 (1968), asked what optics would do if ε and μ were both negative: a left-handed medium, a reversed Doppler shift, and a slab that acts as a lens. Pendry, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85, 3966 (2000), showed the same slab can amplify evanescent waves and beat the diffraction limit. The plate traces geometric rays through n < 0, not a fabricated metamaterial.

Evidence covers only the documented domain in validation/VESELAGO.md and the veselago-science / veselago-print-state results artifacts: the geometric ray trace, the drawn rays, the n = −1 image metric and the print path.

The status line reports a focus only for the textbook image. It reads "Veselago focus" when n = −1, the source is closer than the slab is thick, and an unclamped exit line crosses the axis behind the back face. Any other real crossing is "image behind the slab". No such crossing is "no image behind the slab". Over the 59,200-configuration sweep this agrees with the independent crossings, including the 16,496 in-domain plates with no crossing behind the slab (none labelled a focus). At n ≠ −1, on all 40,768 sweep plates with a crossing behind the slab, the line gives the nearest and farthest of those crossings (within 1e-9 px of the independent trace) and the paraxial point L/|n| − d. It does not say the rays meet there. The Δx/W number is the brightest point against 2L − d, and it is printed only at n = −1.

When the back face lies beyond the last drawn column (grid 128 or 144 with a thick slab and a distant source: 2,368 sweep plates), the ray stops instead of walking backwards to W − 2. Those plates have no stray ink. They stay outside the vertex comparison, because the end point at W − 2 is not drawn.

Transmitted geometric rays only: no Fresnel reflection, wave optics, evanescent-wave amplification (Pendry), absorption or dispersion. At n = −0.40, rays with |sin θ| > 0.4 have no transmitted ray and are skipped entirely, incident segment included: 2 of 12, 4 of 28, 6 of 48 and 6 of 64 rays. The status line names that count. The reflected rays are not drawn.
Refocusing at n = −1 (slab0 + d inside, slab0 + 2L − d behind) is a geometric identity of the flat slab. It is recorded as a regression check, not a prediction.
Hash-only indices between −0.43497 and −0.4 reach the 0.05 slope clamp (veselago.js:88) for near-grazing rays: 322.85 px vertex error at n = −0.43527. These indices are outside the domain.

Plus 2,931 seeded continuous-valued configurations with n from −2.2 to −0.44. Checked per ray: entry, exit and end vertices, axis crossings and total-reflection drops, plus lit cells against the traced rays. n = −1: inside and behind images over 4,440 layouts and the brightest-point metric over 2,412. Closed-form crossings, paraxial image and aberration at n −0.8, −1.2, −1.5, −2.2, −0.4 and +1.5. The status words are checked against those crossings on every sweep plate.
numerical.criteria: Vertices, crossings and layout within 1e-9 px of the reference. Identical total-reflection sets. Zero lit cells more than half a cell from every traced ray, and every ray segment inks at least 70% of its eligible columns. n = −1: every crossing within 1e-9 px of slab0 + d and slab0 + 2L − d, and no crossing behind the slab when d > L. Where L − d ≥ 5 and the image lies at or before W − 5, the brightest point is within 2.5 px of slab0 + 2L − d and the recorded peak equals the independent window maximum. n ≠ −1: crossings within 1e-9 px of the closed form. The innermost ray is within twice the third-order term of the paraxial image L/|n| − d. The aberration has the sign of 1/n² − 1, and the brightest point lies inside the crossing range ± 2.5 px.
numerical.benchmark: Independent vector Snell refraction at both faces. The tangential wavevector is continuous, n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2, so n2 < 0 puts the refracted ray on the incident side of the normal while energy leaves the interface. Line-plane and line-axis intersections, and the closed-form flat-slab crossing L|tan θ2|/|tan θ| − d with paraxial limit L/|n| − d.
numerical.failureControl: n = +1 is rejected: no ray crosses the axis behind the slab, and the brightest point is 21.99 px from 2L − d. A wrong-sign refraction (46.37 px vertex error at n = −1) and an exit ray that keeps the slab angle (88.26 px) are rejected at every tested n. An inverted index ratio (sin θ2 = n sin θ) is identical at n = −1 and rejected only at n −0.8, −1.2 and −1.5 (10.70 to 26.78 px), which is why n = −1 alone is not evidence. The n = −1.2 preset is 9.94 px from 2L − d and fails the 2.5 px image predicate.

The status words name a real crossing behind the slab, and call it a Veselago focus only at n = −1 with d < L. At other n the line gives the crossing range and the paraxial point L/|n| − d, and does not call that one image. A back face past the last drawn column stops the ray; those plates are outside the vertex comparison. Hash-only near-grazing indices are outside the domain.

reference: H. F. Talbot, Phil. Mag. 9, 401 (1836). A periodic grating, lit coherently, revives as a sharp image at the Talbot distance z_T = 2 d²/λ and as a half-period image at z_T/2 = d²/λ. Depth on this plate is in units of d²/λ, so slider value 2 is one Talbot length and 1 is the half-period image. Between them the near field is a carpet of fractional revivals.

reference: Ernst Ising, Z. Phys. 31, 253 (1925); Lars Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944); Nicholas Metropolis, Arianna W. Rosenbluth, Marshall N. Rosenbluth, Augusta H. Teller and Edward Teller, J. Chem. Phys. 21, 1087 (1953). Ising solved the chain and found no transition. Onsager solved the square lattice exactly and found one at T_c = 2/ln(1+√2). The Metropolis algorithm samples the Boltzmann distribution by proposing single flips and accepting them with probability min(1, exp(−ΔE/T)). Here the lattice is updated as a checkerboard: two half-sweeps per step, each parity with its neighbors held fixed, so the GPU can flip every site of one color at once.
equation: E = −J Σ⟨ij⟩ sᵢsⱼ − h Σᵢ sᵢ,   P(flip) = min(1, e^{−ΔE/T}),   T_c = 2/ln(1+√2) ≈ 2.269

T_c agrees with Onsager at 0.13% through the Binder fixed-point estimator, which assumes the universal U* = 0.61069; the model-free crossing between grid sizes is inconclusive in quick mode.

Since recipe v3 (2026-09-24) each seed's Metropolis numbers come from its own keyed stream (siteHashKeyed); tools/ising-science.js shows two seeds whose shared-stream windows coincide run identical chains on the shared stream (site agreement 1.0000) and independent ones on the keyed stream (0.5046). Recipes older than v3 keep the shared stream through legacy, where seeds read windows of one hash sequence; the tool still allocates disjoint windows.

Since 2026-09-24 the status line compares |m| with Yang only for a cold (ordered) start at h = 0 below 0.95 T_c; a hot or split start below T_c coarsens and can sit in a stripe state, so it prints |m| with its error bar and a note instead of a comparison.

reference: D. J. Thouless, Phys. Rev. B 27, 6083 (1983). An adiabatic cycle of a 1D insulator pumps a quantized charge equal to the Chern number of the (k, t) torus. Rice and Mele (1982) wrote the two-band lattice that makes the winding visible. The plate is the occupied-band density versus cycle angle; the centre of mass walks one cell when the loop in (u, v, δ) encloses the origin, and stands still when it does not.
equation: P(φ) = (1/2π) ∮ A(k,φ) dk,   ΔP over a cycle = C₁ ∈ ℤ
limitations: Status is unvalidated. The plate does not compute ΔP. src/modules/thouless.js draws a cartoon density. Its pol() drops the imaginary part of the overlap, so that sum is not a Berry phase, and the status line only names the chosen cycle. An unused metric is hardcoded to 1 or 0. Neither is the Thouless pump.

numerical.scope: Independent Float64 Rice-Mele Hamiltonian, not the studio plate. Fukui-Hatsugai-Suzuki Chern number of the occupied band on a 32 by 32 (k, phi) mesh, occupied-band Berry curvature on a 96 by 96 mesh, and the Resta center of mass of the filled band on a periodic ring of 16 unit cells. Enclosing cycle, offset cycle, reversed cycle, frozen Hamiltonian, and one diabatic schedule.
numerical.criteria: Enclosing Fukui-Hatsugai-Suzuki Chern number within 1e-8 of +1 on both 32 by 32 and 16 by 16 meshes; curvature integral within 1e-4 of that integer; Bloch residual of the real-space matrix below 1e-9. Slow schedule (period 40, step 0.5) center of mass and bond current each within 0.02 of +1. Offset cycle Chern number within 1e-8 of 0 and must fail a predicate that requires absolute Chern number 1. Fast schedule (period 4, step 0.05) center of mass at least 0.15 from every integer, and step 0.025 must not restore an integer. Dropping the imaginary part of the spinor must miss +1. A frozen Hamiltonian must pump less than 1e-6.
numerical.benchmark: Occupied band of H(k) = (v + w cos k) sigma_x + (w sin k) sigma_y + delta sigma_z. The lattice Chern number is the Fukui-Hatsugai-Suzuki sum, checked against the skyrmion integral of the d vector (lower band) and against the winding of (v - w, delta) about the gap closing at the origin. The pumped charge is the many-body Resta center of mass, checked against the integrated bond current. The bulk gap is twice the minimum of |d|.
numerical.failureControl: The offset cycle winds zero times and its Chern number is 0, so the absolute-value-1 predicate fails. The period-4 schedule has center of mass 0.827 at step 0.05 and 0.827 at step 0.025, so the integer predicate fails and halving the step does not repair it. Reversing phi sends the Chern number from +1 to -1. Zeroing the imaginary part of the spinor, the plate's overlap, returns Chern number 0. Holding the Hamiltonian fixed returns a center of mass of 0.
numerical.limitations: Not the plate. The plate does not compute ΔP. No print comparison. The fast center of mass (0.827) and bond current (0.766) differ by 0.061 because the Resta modulus falls to 0.395; both miss every integer. The slow ring charge is 1.00047, not a mathematical 1.

reference: Henri Bénard, Revue générale des Sciences pures et appliquées 11, 1261 (1900), saw the cells in a thin layer of spermaceti heated from below. reference: The sea is Swift and Hohenberg, Phys. Rev. A 15, 319 (1977). The brightness after a thin phase screen is Berry’s catastrophe optics, the ray map x ↦ x + s ∇h. Intensity writing a height is the photothermal / Marangoni class. Laser-induced surface patterns are already modelled with Swift–Hohenberg (Rudenko, Colombier, Itina, Stoian, Phys. Rev. The wavelength is the power-weighted mean of the 5-point Laplacian symbol with the field mean removed, converted to the wavelength of an axis mode with the same symbol. reference: Crapper, An exact solution for progressive capillary waves of arbitrary amplitude, J. Fluid Mech. 2, 532 (1957), found the unique closed-form finite-amplitude pure-capillary wave on deep water: crests flatten, troughs sharpen, and at s* ≈ 0.730 the trough pinches a bubble of air. The free surface drawn here is that classical map, denominator 1+A²+2A cos. It first stands vertical at A = √2−1 on a shoulder and the trough self-touches at A* ≈ 0.455. Hur and Vanden-Broeck, Eur. Recipes older than v7 keep the previous plate, whose denominator was 1+A²−2A cos: that curve overturns at the trough at A = 3−2√2 and self-crosses near A = 0.30, and it is not this bubble. This plate is a seeded print of the exact map. It is not a new equation.

reference: Equal-pair three-vortex collapse (formerly "Three-vortex collapse bound"): an explicit formula and sharp minimum for a classical three-vortex collapse family, the one with two equal circulations, independently derived in this project with AI assistance. Circulations Γ = (1, 1, −1/2), positions z₁ = 0, z₂ = 1, z₃ = 1/2 + (√3/2) e^{iθ} on the L = 0 circle, 0 < θ < π/2. θ is the third vortex's place on that circle, not an interior angle. ω₀ t_c = (2 − cos²θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ √2, equality uniquely at tan θ = 1/√2 (interior angles 22.5°, 45°, 112.5°). With u = tan θ the product is u + 1/(2u), and ω₀ t_c − √2 = (√2 u − 1)² / (2u) ≥ 0. At θ = 45° the product is 3/2. Three-vortex collapse is Gröbli (1877). Aref, Phys. Fluids 22, 057104 (2010), gives rotation and collapse separately and writes their product as the pitch of the log spiral. The formula explicitly specializes and reparameterizes the spiral coefficient in Gröbli (1877), section 10. Kimura, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 56, 2024 (1987), section 4, gives the collapse and rotation rates A and B in this same parametrization, for circulations (2, 2, −1), and their ratio B/(−2A) is this formula; he minimizes the collision time instead, at cos 2θ = 3/5, where the product is 3/2, the value it also takes at θ = 45°. It was independently derived here and recorded on 2026-09-19. Priority of the optimized minimum remains unconfirmed; see identities/ORIGINALITY-FOLLOWUP.md, identities/NOVELTY-AUDIT.md and IDENTITIES.md. Cite as Equal-pair three-vortex collapse. If the vortices leave the circle, or the kernel is wrong, the ratio against √2 misses and the status line marks miss. The picture still draws. Custom takes any three circulations and positions, computes their Biot-Savart velocities in the same convention, and tests the classical conditions for self-similar collapse, Σ ΓᵢΓⱼ = 0 and zero angular impulse about the center of vorticity (Gröbli 1877; Aref, Phys. Fluids 22, 393 (1979) and 057104 (2010)). Its normalization, circulations (1, μ, −μ/(1+μ)) on the zero-impulse circle, is that of Gotoda, J. Dyn. Differ. Equ. 33, 1759 (2021). The bound P = |ω₀| t_c > √3/2 over every three-vortex collapse, printed beside a custom collapse, is from this project's paper Minimal Winding in the Self-Similar Collapse of Point Vortices (papers/minimal-winding), which has not been peer reviewed; its Remark 2 is this family's √2, and √3/2 is the infimum over every three-vortex collapse, approached but not attained.

reference: A closed form and sharp minimum for the scale-invariant product on the classical four-vortex parallelogram collapse family, independently derived in this project with AI assistance. Circulations Γ = (1, 1, −2 − √3, −2 − √3), diagonals in ratio √(2 + √3), angle θ between the diagonals, 0 < θ < π/2. |ω₀| t_c = (√3/4)(4 − cos 2θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ 3√5/4, equality uniquely at cos 2θ = 1/4; in the collapsing orientation used here ω₀ < 0, so the product is taken unsigned. With φ = 2θ the quotient is (4 − cos φ)/sin φ, and the critical point is cos φ = 1/4. Four-vortex parallelogram collapse is Novikov and Sedov, Sov. Phys. JETP 50, 297 (1979). Gotoda, arXiv:2002.09624 (2020 preprint), eq. (3.13), gives the collapse rate A(θ) and the spin B(θ) separately after those authors. The product |B|/(2|A|) (A < 0 on the collapsing branch, and B = ω₀ < 0 in the orientation used here) simplifies to the formula above. It is Proposition 2 with n = 2 of the paper Minimal Winding in the Self-Similar Collapse of Point Vortices. The formula and minimum were derived here and recorded on 2026-09-20. Historical priority is unconfirmed; see identities/NOVELTY-AUDIT.md and IDENTITIES.md. The reciprocal pair Γ = (1, 1, −2 + √3, −2 + √3) is the same family with the diagonals swapped. If the vortices leave the parallelogram, or the kernel is wrong, the ratio against 3√5/4 misses and the status line marks miss. The picture still draws.
equation: |ω₀| t_c = (√3/4)(4 − cos 2θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ 3√5/4  on the Novikov–Sedov parallelogram;  equality at cos 2θ = 1/4

reference: A closed form and sharp minimum for the scale-invariant product on a classical five-vortex collapse family, independently derived in this project with AI assistance. Circulations Γ = (−1, −1, 1/2, 1/2, −3/4), four vortices at the vertices of a parallelogram whose diagonals meet at the fifth, diagonals in ratio 1/√2, angle θ between the diagonals, 0 < θ < π/2. |ω₀| t_c = (3/16)(7 − 4 cos 2θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ 3√33/16, equality uniquely at cos 2θ = 4/7; in the collapsing orientation used here ω₀ < 0, so the product is taken unsigned. With φ = 2θ the quotient is (7 − 4 cos φ)/sin φ, and the critical point is cos φ = 4/7. Five-vortex parallelogram-plus-center collapse is Novikov and Sedov, Sov. Phys. JETP 50, 297 (1979). Gotoda, arXiv:2002.09624 (2020 preprint), eq. (3.13), gives the collapse rate A(θ) and the spin B(θ) separately after those authors, and plots this family (γ1 = −1, γ2 = 1/2, γ3 = −3/4) as Hamiltonian against collapse rate. The product |B|/(2|A|) (A < 0 on the collapsing branch, and B = ω₀ < 0 in the orientation used here) on that slice simplifies to the formula above. It is the example after Proposition 3 of the paper Minimal Winding in the Self-Similar Collapse of Point Vortices. The formula and minimum were derived here and recorded on 2026-09-20. Historical priority is unconfirmed; see identities/NOVELTY-AUDIT.md and IDENTITIES.md. The reciprocal pair with the diagonals swapped is the same family. If the vortices leave the quincunx, or the kernel is wrong, the ratio against 3√33/16 misses and the status line marks miss. The picture still draws. This is not Novikov and Sedov's t_* or ω separately under a new name, and it is not the four-vortex parallelogram lock.
equation: |ω₀| t_c = (3/16)(7 − 4 cos 2θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ 3√33/16  on the Novikov–Sedov five-vortex quincunx;  equality at cos 2θ = 4/7

reference: D. J. Pinto and G. B. Ermentrout, Spatially structured activity in synaptically coupled neuronal networks: I. Traveling fronts and pulses, SIAM J. Appl. Math. 62, 206–225 (2001), eq. (3) with the feedback decay set to zero; S. Amari, Dynamics of pattern formation in lateral-inhibition type neural fields, Biol. Cybern. 27, 77–87 (1977). The pulse speeds compared at β = 20, θ = 1/4, ε = 1/10 and at β = 12, θ = 1/4, ε = 3/20 are computer-assisted enclosures drafted in this repository (papers/nf-pulse). Original implementation of established equations.
limitations: The comparison covers two parameter points only, beta = 20, theta = 1/4, eps = 1/10 and beta = 12, theta = 1/4, eps = 3/20 (gamma = 0, kernel e^-|x|/2), with a central kick (six kick shapes at the first point, the default shape at the second), rings of 240 and 400, and the shipped cells (1,024, 2,048, 4,096) and steps (0.1, 0.05, 0.025). At every other parameter the timed speed is printed as a measurement with no reference and no error estimate.

The reference speeds are computer-assisted enclosures of width 1e-25 drafted in this repository (papers/nf-pulse and papers/nf-pulse/ext/gain-12), computed in ball arithmetic from the traveling-wave ODE by programs separate from this tab. The lemmas those proofs rest on do not yet have written proofs (papers/nf-pulse/notes/QUALITY.md).

The error estimate |K| dx^4 + |Kt| dt^4 uses constants measured by the benchmark's own refinement at each point (K = -9.19e-3 and -2.84e-3, Kt = -1.0e-3 and -7.1e-4); the witness allows twice it plus 2e-8. The Richardson limits sit 9.1e-10 and 2.3e-10 from the proved speeds.

That the plate settles onto the fast pulse is observed, not proved: stability of the fast pulse is not established (papers/nf-pulse/ext/stability). The slow pulse proved at the first point is expected to be unstable; kicks at the launch threshold hesitate at a front speed near 0.1 and then die or accelerate to the fast pulse, an observation at one kick width.

The timing rules (a front clear of other crossings, kick sites and disturbed medium for 42 units ahead, kick sites behind excluded within the larger of their half-width and 20 kernel lengths, isolated after covering the ahead distance, timed from 30 time units after its birth over at least 20) are heuristics checked on the stated fixtures. The behind margin uses the symmetric kernel decay exp(-20)/2, about 1e-9, not a proved speed-error bound. A residue below the 1e-7 rest tolerance ahead can still move the speed by a few times 1e-8.

No print-accuracy evidence is registered. The plate is a Catmull-Rom display of a Float32 record of u and v (at most 2,048 columns and 1,536 rows); prints add pixels, not resolution. Periodic ring only: no two-dimensional field, synaptic delay, recovery decay (gamma), noise or heterogeneity.

reference: R. A. Fisher, The wave of advance of advantageous genes, Annals of Eugenics 7, 355 (1937); A. N. Kolmogorov, I. G. Petrovsky and N. S. Piskunov, Bulletin of Moscow University, Mathematics and Mechanics 1, 1 (1937). A front started from a bounded patch travels at the minimal speed 2√(rD) only in the long run: Maury Bramson, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 31, 531 (1978), showed a straight front lags by (3/2)√(D/r) ln t, so its speed is 2√(rD) − (3/2)√(D/r)/t; Ute Ebert and Wim van Saarloos, Physica D 146, 1 (2000), found the next term; Jürgen Gärtner, Mathematische Nachrichten 105, 317 (1982), gave the circular front in two dimensions, which lags by 2√(D/r) ln t. Habitats of varying quality follow Nanako Shigesada, Kohkichi Kawasaki and Ei Teramoto, Theoretical Population Biology 30, 143 (1986).
equation: ∂u/∂t = D∇²u + r u(1 − u),   minimal front speed 2√(rD)
limitations: Deterministic single-species logistic reaction-diffusion on a closed (zero-flux) plate: no demographic noise, Allee effect, advection or genetic drift. The territory view maps first arrival, not genetics. A population illustration does not establish experimental accuracy.

The status-line front speed is read from the arrival-time field (mean 1/|∇T| over clean cells in the last half of the arrivals) and is compared with 2√(rD) with basis deterministic. It sits below 2√(rD) by the finite-time lag, which the note prints: Bramson's (3/2)√(D/r)/t for a straight front and 2√(D/r)/t for a circle. The circular coefficient 2 was not read in Gärtner (1982) or Ducrot (2015); it agrees with Bramson's 3/2 plus the curvature term, and its next correction and the founder-radius effect are unknown, so the plate criterion for circles is a band.

The grid effect printed on the status line is the difference from a twin on cells twice as large; with the 9-point stencil at D dt/h² = 1/6 the straight-front speed converges at fourth order, and the difference overstates the plate's own error.
Heterogeneous habitats (patchy, hostile islands) print no comparison and are not benchmarked beyond the scheme.

reference: Carlo Cattaneo, Atti del Seminario Matematico e Fisico della Università di Modena 3, 83 (1948), and Pierre Vernotte, Comptes Rendus de l’Académie des Sciences 246, 3154 (1958), gave the heat flux a relaxation time τ, τ ∂q/∂t + q = −α∇T, so that heat released at a point spreads at the finite speed √(α/τ) instead of everywhere at once. With the energy balance it is the telegraph equation. The linear, constant-coefficient form here is the simplest member of the family; the proposal this tab follows points to Róbert Kovács and Patrizia Rogolino, Numerical treatment of nonlinear Fourier and Maxwell-Cattaneo-Vernotte heat transport equations, arXiv:1910.09175 (2019), whose nonlinear, temperature-dependent coefficients this tab does not include.
equation: τ ∂²T/∂t² + ∂T/∂t = α∇²T  (linear, constant coefficients),   τ s² + s + α k² = 0
limitations: Linear, constant-coefficient Maxwell-Cattaneo-Vernotte (telegraph) model with unit heat capacity on a periodic plate, a labeled simplification of the nonlinear equations of Kovács and Rogolino (arXiv:1910.09175). No temperature-dependent coefficients, boundaries, material data or Guyer-Krumhansl terms; not a material model, and no claim about which solids conduct heat this way. The model lets the temperature dip below ambient behind a front, a known objection to it.

The status line compares the plate's (1, 0) Fourier coefficient per unit heat with the exact solution of τ s² + s + α k² = 0 for the same deposits (basis deterministic) and prints Fourier's law alone beside it. Only the lowest mode is used: far below k_c it is nearly Fourier (on Rings and glow, k/k_c = 0.22, Fourier misses by only 1.5e-3), so the check says less about τ there. Total heat is a construction regression.

Deposits add the half-step flux +tanh(dt/2τ)α∇(deposit) so that new heat starts at rest; without it the check missed by 3e-4. More than four deposits in one step are carried to the next step and the bookkeeping records the step used.

Continuum-reference measured ratios 0.9955, 0.9662, 0.8962 include a 10% failure at τ = 0.001 from the amplified spatial offset; the discrete-reference ratios are 1.012, 1.019, 1.055.

reference: A computer-assisted proof that the equal double pendulum (m = l = g = 1, bottom rest at energy -3) has a transversal homoclinic orbit at E = -1/2, 0 and 1/2 is drafted in this repository, research/double-pendulum/REPORT.md. It is published as version 1.0.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22997540. The horseshoe and the positive entropy are the theorem of Stephen Smale, Diffeomorphisms with many periodic points, in Differential and Combinatorial Topology, Princeton University Press (1965), incorporating the homoclinic construction of George D. Birkhoff, On the periodic motions of dynamical systems, Acta Mathematica 50 (1927) 359-379. This plate is a floating-point picture of that tangle. The proof is the interval computation.
equation: H = (p₁² + 2 p₂² − 2 cos(θ₁−θ₂) p₁ p₂) / (2D) − 2 cos θ₁ − cos θ₂,  D = 1 + sin²(θ₁−θ₂);  section θ₁ = 0, θ₁′ > 0
limitations: Float64 classical RK4 picture of the equal double pendulum (m = l = g = 1, bottom rest at E = -3). It does not rerun the interval proof. A crossing drawn on the section is a picture, not a proved crossing.

Any other energy is outside the proof and is labeled that way. From the report seed the symmetric family is not found at E = -0.75; the plate then draws the sea only.

numerical.scope: Selected exact single-Gaussian paths, one five-component spiral mixture, continuity residual, RK4 refinement, eight independent seeds of2048 particles.
numerical.criteria: Exact path error below1e-6 at64 steps with refinement ratios above10; continuity residual below1e-7; mixture refinement ratios above8; five target moments within6 standard errors across8 seeds.
numerical.benchmark: Exact single-Gaussian trajectory t*mu+sqrt((1-t)^2+t^2*sigma^2)*z; closed-form Gaussian-mixture density, mean and second moments.
numerical.failureControl: Sign-flipped velocity fails the continuity residual; untransported standard-normal samples fail the identical target-moment acceptance predicate.
numerical.limitations: One mixture and selected paths, no learned model or physical experiment. Conservative six-standard-error moment gate is not a simultaneous confidence certificate.

print.scope: Three static recipes, actual2400 square pixel module PNG/SVG exports, every Float64 trajectory word, finite values, recipe and deterministic replay. The default and five presets also pass tools/export.js through the real UI.
print.criteria: Dimensions2400x2400, nonblank raster, exact data/state preservation and replay, one circle perparticle plus one path perparticle when trails are enabled; deliberate changed trajectory must fail.
print.limitations: One Chrome renderer and three recipes; no calibrated-color, scientific generalization or learned-model-quality claim.
